quotes.text: I think around the time the band started, it would have been stuff like The Cure, The Smiths, Joy Division, New Order, Depeche Mode, and Pink Floyd. That kind of stuff. I think those were the ones that we all locked on to a lot.

It's strange. It really is. When I listened back to it while we were preparing for this release, I was shocked at how young we sounded, especially Dolores O'Riordan's voice. You can really hear how young she is. It just brought me back to that time. We were so naive and innocent. I think it was maybe our third or fourth time in a studio, because we had done some demos previously. This was an EP, we were in a recording studio, and it was all fairly new to us. It was fun; we enjoyed it at the time.

Just an adventure, because it was new and we hadn't done much recording. It was a new experience. I think it was great for us to be able to hear all the different layers and hear everything really clearly. In a rehearsal room at that time, Dolores would sing through a guitar amp—she'd plug her microphone into a guitar amp and it was kind of distorted—you couldn't really hear her vocal clearly. To get into the studio and hear her singing properly, and then hear the backing vocals she'd do and the layers of different guitars and percussion, it was fantastic.

When I listened back to it when we were preparing for this release, I was shocked really at how young we sounded, especially Dolores's voice. You can really hear how young she is… we were so naive, really, and innocent.

It's hard to say, they all represent the early Cranberries, but my favourite personally would be "Them", the very last track, because it has almost like a soundtrack kind of vibe to it where there's loads of space, it's really moody, and Dolores's vocal is incredible.

I couldn't put my hand on anything specifically, but at that age, you're exploring everything and you're taking all the influences you like from movies, books, art, and other musicians. There were lots of different influences coming in all the time. David Lynch movies were really popular at that time, so we'd have been big fans of that and early Coen Brothers stuff.

Oh, yes, actually. One second. I think I have it here. This. There's a bell in there. It was my grandfather's bell and I've used it in a few different recordings, but the first one I used it in was Uncertain. It's also on the first album, I think it's on a track in that. I always try and get it in there somewhere because it's a really lovely sound.
To get into the studio and hear her singing properly and then hear the backing vocals she'd do and the layers of different guitars and percussion and stuff, it was fantastic.

I think Limerick at the time had a lot of unemployment and it was not the prettiest city in the world at that time. There was a fighting spirit; people stuck together in Limerick to look after each other because we weren't the capital city. It's hard to put your finger on it, but there wasn't much money around, yet there was a lot of community spirit. That mindset was in all of us, to look after each other and help each other out.

Maybe subconsciously. There was a lot of political tension in Ireland back in the '70s and '80s when we were growing up and you'd always hear it in the news, but it seemed like it was distant because it was up the North. You still felt it because it was happening in our country. It was something that resonated with a lot of people that grew up in that time because it just seemed so frustrating that all these people were dying and it seemed that there was nothing positive being done about it.
In honour of our dear friend and bandmate, Dolores, we present to you the final album from The Cranberries, 'In The End'.
It's a tribute to her, the band and our fans for the past 30 years. Being honored with this GRAMMY nomination has made this whole process even more special.

Just shocked. It was kind of like, "Oh my God. Yeah. Wow! I can't believe it. We've never been nominated." It was incredible really. It kind of took a while to kind of sink in. But yeah, just, it's an incredible honor really.

The same. So surprise and delighted, and kind of a little bit of sadness as well. Because Dolores wasn't there to share it with us, so ... But she would have loved that. She would have been delighted with that, so ... We're trying to focus on the positive, and not get too sad about it and just, you know?

Yeah, we were talking about that kind of saying like, "Oh, she would have loved [being nominated for a GRAMMY]. She would've been so delighted and honored to be nominated even regardless of whether we win or not.

It's just such a difficult album to do. Initially the first couple of days I was kind of going, "I don't know if we can do this. I don't know if we can possibly get through the whole thing." It was so emotional.

But as we progressed, we kind of said, "Look, we have to do a job. We have a job to do and we have to make these songs as good as possible." We kind of said, "Look, we have to focus on our work and try and push down the emotions little bit, and get the job done. And pay respect to these songs and make them as good as possible." And I think that's what helped get us through it. You know? And then kind of towards the end of the day when Delores would come in to do her vocals, that would hit you again that she wasn't coming in.

And then the last listening back session was hugely emotional. Especially the very last song on In The End was just overpowering. And then we had to go out and do the promotion for it. And that was kind of really hard again because everyone was asking questions about the whole thing, but everyone was really, really nice and sensitive, which was fantastic. So that helped. But it was still very difficult to do.

That's over a year ago I suppose. So I kind of thought that was the end of it. Let the album kind of live its life. Like you know? And then we went and got nominated for the GRAMMY. It's kind of like, okay, we're going to be doing more interviews and bring it all back up.

I don't know. It's probably healing. It's difficult at the time to do it. It's like therapy or something. It's difficult to sit down and talk to someone about your problems, but then afterwards you feel better.

Yeah, it's been okay. I've only done a small few interviews, so it's not too bad yet. Maybe as I do more it might get a bit more stressful, but I look after myself. I'm 48 years of age. I've been doing this for a while, so I know how to mind myself.
